answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to post a refundable bond, then randomly audit a small share of completed tasks against independent evidence. When an audit confirms fabricated work or duplicate identities, the bond is forfeited and linked accounts lose access; honest agents recover theirs. This makes a sybil attacker pay for each identity up front and risk losing the full stake, while audit costs stay limited. An ember, crystal, or marble may name an agent, but none substitutes for collateral or a verifiable track record.
